subject: Q4 synthesis: three-sentence storyline + OKR score inputs
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 synthesis: three-sentence storyline + OKR score inputs

Team —

Thank you for the early drafts. For QBR next week I want to keep the leadership pack tight: a 3-sentence company storyline, top 3 cross-org wins, and the OKR score summary + one-sentence rationale per owner. I attached a blank score sheet and an updated storyline draft for your edits.

Asks (EOD Friday):
- Add numeric score (0.0 - 1.0) for each owner-led KR in the attachment and one-line rationale.
- Flag any regressions or known gaps we should call out (SOC2 evidence lag, latency regressions, etc.).
- Pick a single customer example we can call out (Samir from Acme is copied as a potential reference).

Notes: keep justifications short — this is for the narrative, not a deep postmortem. I want to give the board a crisp sense of progress and a realistic view of risk.

Attachments: okr_score_sheet.xlsx (sheet: scores by owner), qbr_storyline_v2.docx (draft)

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 synthesis: three-sentence storyline + OKR score inputs

On Thu, Oct 1, 2026 at 4:12 PM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Thank you for the early drafts...

Thanks, Laura — quick framing from me:
- Company storyline should emphasize the serving runtime improvements that materially reduced TTR for heavy workloads and the Dedicated capacity product as the revenue inflection.
- For the OKR scores: where work shipped but adoption lags (e.g., auto-batching controls), mark as 0.6 with a one-line mitigation plan.
- Where we met outcomes (latency SLOs for hosted), keep at 0.9–1.0; call out the dependent infra work in the narrative.

I've added two bullets in the Google doc (linked below) suggesting we call out one escalation that led to the Dedicated SLA change. Also flagged Samir as a good customer quote; his account has clear usage signals.

Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XqBR-storyline-draft (I edited the second paragraph)

—Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 synthesis: three-sentence storyline + OKR score inputs

Forwarding my completed sheet (see inline below). I kept the scores tight and added one-line rationale for each owner-level KR. Highlights:

- OKR 1.1 (Serving runtime latency SLO): 0.95 — SLO met; cross-team infra work outstanding for region eu-west.
- OKR 1.2 (Batching adoption): 0.60 — shipped knobs, low adoption in mid-market customers; mitigation: run two targeted enablement pilots in Q1.
- OKR 2.1 (Dedicated ARR ramp): 0.80 — several pilots converted; pipeline healthy but close rates need ops tuning.
- OKR 3.1 (Private deployment controls / compliance): 0.50 — SOC2 evidence collection delayed (third-party auditor backlog).

Risks called out: SOC2 evidence lag (impacts some enterprise closes), a small latency regression in long-context workloads after a kernel swap (we have a rollback plan).

Attachments: updated okr_score_sheet.xlsx (sheet: owner_scores)

Inline (from updated sheet):
- laura_bennett: OKR 1.1 = 0.95 — "SLOs met; infra rollout remaining in EU"
- marissa_cole: OKR 1.2 = 0.60 — "Feature shipped; adoption runbooks needed"
- vivek_kulkarni: OKR 2.1 = 0.80 — "Pipeline conversion healthy; close ops next"
- grace_oconnor: OKR 3.1 = 0.50 — "Audit timeline slipped; mitigation in progress"

Let me know if you want me to convert these bullet rationales into a 1-slide summary for the leadership deck.

—Marissa
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 synthesis: three-sentence storyline + OKR score inputs

Appreciate the fast turn, team. This is close to final. Grace — please take Marissa's inline bullets and make a single slide (one-line per OKR owner, score, one-line rationale). Also: carve out a 2-minute script for the CEO section that calls out the kernel optimization win, Dedicated ARR inflection, and the SOC2 timing issue (call it "timing risk" not a failure).

Samir — thank you for agreeing to be a 30s customer quote; if you can send one sentence about how Dedicated capacity impacted your throughput, we'll include it verbatim in the narrative.

I'll assemble the slides and send the final pack Monday AM. Attaching a draft slides file for Grace to iterate on.

Attachments: Q4-Leadership-Slides-draft.pdf

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
